issue.title: Move isOldMssql function to Connection class

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
`yii\db\mssql\QueryBuilder::isOldMssql()` reads a PDO attribute to get the database version, but some database drivers (e.g. dblib) do not support getting attributes and this causes an error:

```
Uncaught exception 'PDOException' with message 'SQLSTATE[IM001]: Driver does not support this function: driver does not support getting attributes' in ... 
```

Moving `isOldMssql()` to the `Connection` class makes it easier to override in a subclass, allowing a person to simply return true if they know the database involved in the connection is an old version of MSSQL.  I think that  this function is more of an attribute of the connection than the query, so it makes more sense here anyway.

body: Is it better to add this in the extended PDO class or should we just do this fallback in the `isOldMssql` method?

I put this in the PDO extended class because the `isOldMssql` is using a PDO method to get server version, and I thought it could be useful to have a generic method to get server version.

Anyway, shouldn't the query result be cached ? `isOldMssql` is called each time a query is build. I don't know for other PDO drivers, but in case of `dblib`, it will make a supplemental SQL query for every query
@tof06 can you send a PR with your solution and add caching of the value in QueryBuilder?
Yes I can ! But I won't be able to make it until next Tuesday.

I'm not sure on how to implement caching... Which cache should I use ? The global `cache` component ? The db `Connection` query or schema cache ? 

And, why just cache the value in QueryBuilder and not in `GetAttribute` method ?
I guess what @cebe meant is just to store the result in a variable so that it can be reused by other queries later.
@qiangxue I see, but it means that the value will be cached only for the current request.
Yeah. I think we can improve it gradually if later we find this causes big performance hit.
